lines.trans: Hey, Baek Seung-chan, are you just getting back now?
Where is Joon-mo?
He went straight to the team dinner venue.
I stopped by briefly to drop off my bags before heading over.
Hey, you are on a drinking ban—how can you go to a team dinner?
I told you not to drink for the time being because you have to watch your mouth!
It is a full-team dinner celebrating our first shoot, so there is no way I can skip it.

words.gloss: because it is a team dinner

lines.trans: I will avoid drinking alcohol as much as possible.
That makes me nervous, though.

That makes me nervous, though.
Where is your team having dinner?
Goodbye!

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (interj).

examples.trans: Hey, Baek Seung-chan, are you just getting back now?
Here the word for 'hey' is key.

meanings.note: Emphasizes a change of state or that a new moment has arrived (contrasting with 지금 'right this second').

examples.trans: I have to go home now.
The performance is starting very soon now.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.
We have a team dinner today.
Where is the company dinner?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: He went straight to the team dinner venue.
Here the word for 'to the venue' is key.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to emphasize immediate action or result.
E.g., 바로 옆 ('right next to'), 바로 그 사람 ('that very person').

examples.trans: I'll start right away now.
The cafe is right in front of the school.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

examples.text: 어제는 술 먹고 들이닥친 거고 오늘은 짐 들어 준 거잖아.
examples.trans: Yesterday he barged in drunk, and today he just carried my bags.

examples.text: 우리 가위바위보 해서 서로 짐 들어 주기 할까요?
examples.trans: Shall we play rock-paper-scissors to carry each other's bags?

meanings.en: to have, to possess, to take
meanings.note: Shortened from 가지다.

examples.trans: I have money on me.
Please bring that here (take it and give).

놓다.gloss: to put, to place, to leave

meanings.en: to put, to place, to leave
meanings.note: Often used as an auxiliary verb to indicate leaving something in a certain state.

examples.trans: Please place it on the desk.
I left the door open.

meanings.en: for a moment; briefly; a second
meanings.note: Used to soften requests or indicate a very short duration.

examples.trans: Do you have a moment?
Just a second, I'll be right there.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 저는 짐 갖다 놓고 가려고 잠깐 들렀습니다.
examples.trans: I stopped by briefly to drop off my bags before heading over.
This expression comes from 'stopped by'.

meanings.note: Casual exclamation used to call someone younger or a close friend.

examples.trans: Hey, come quickly!
Hey, where are you going?
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 야, 너 금주 기간인데 회식을 가면 어떡해?
examples.trans: Hey, you are on a drinking ban—how can you go to a team dinner?
Here the word for 'abstaining from alcohol' is key.

examples.text: 수습 기간 중에 세 번 사고 치면 잘릴 수도 있대요.
examples.trans: I heard that if you cause trouble three times during probation, you can get fired.
The topic of period, term came up during this shoot.

meanings.en: what to do, how to act
meanings.note: Contraction of 어떻게 하다.

examples.trans: What should we do?
What should we do? (2)

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 내가 당분간 너 술 먹지 말라 그랬지, 입 조심해야 된다고!
examples.trans: I told you not to drink for the time being because you have to watch your mouth!
Here the word for 'for the time being' is key.
Did you hear about this drinks or something?
I was busy today because of drinks or something.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for eating a meal or food; honorific equivalent is 드시다.

examples.trans: Let's eat lunch together.
Did you eat breakfast?

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: noun mouth

examples.trans: Open mouth.
Mouth hurts.

meanings.note: Used to warn or advise caution.

examples.trans: Please be careful.
Please be careful. (2)

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Prenoun (determiner) placed directly before a noun

examples.trans: Today is my first day at work.
The first snow fell.
Did you hear about this filming too?
I was busy today because of filming too.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 첫 촬영 기념 전체 회식이라 제가 빠질 수가 없습니다.
examples.trans: It is a full-team dinner celebrating our first shoot, so there is no way I can skip it.
Here the word for 'commemoration, celebration' is key.

meanings.en: the whole, the entire thing, all

examples.trans: The entire team worked hard together.
Please check the entire schedule again.

examples.text: 일반인 훈남한테 빠진 톱스타 같은 거네요?
examples.trans: So it's like a top star falling for an ordinary handsome guy?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 빠지다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (fallen for).

meanings.note: Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.
I cannot go today.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.
I understand well (as much as possible).
Today is a (as much as possible) busy day.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.
I'm always anxious before an exam.
I feel a bit uneasy when I'm alone.

meanings.note: Colloquial spoken form of 너희네; used among close friends or to juniors.

examples.text: 너네 오늘 수업 몇 시에 끝나?
examples.trans: What time does your class end today?
You guys all come over here together.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for location.

examples.trans: Where is the restroom?
Where are you right now?

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)
